claims.text: The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy has a superior strength-ductility balance relative to its quaternary and ternary subsets.
The quinary alloy's enhanced mechanical performance arises from a greater propensity for local chemical short-range order.
Local chemical short-range order generates heterogeneous lattice distortions.
The heterogeneous lattice distortions elevate local stacking-fault energies.
The heterogeneous lattice distortions promote dislocation locking.
The heterogeneous lattice distortions promote deformation twinning.
Dislocation locking and twinning delay strain localization and failure.
Thermomechanically processed equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni is single-phase FCC.
The corresponding equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
The compared alloys have similar grain sizes and phase purity.
A broader mix of constituent elements facilitates local short-range ordering in the quinary alloy.
Short-range-order-induced distorted regions act as barriers to dislocation glide.
Barriers to dislocation glide promote dislocation accumulation and the onset of mechanical twinning.
Quaternary and ternary alloys have a lower capacity for local chemical ordering than the quinary alloy.
The quinary alloy will develop a higher density of dislocation locks than the lower-order alloys under identical tests.
The quinary alloy will exhibit more stacking faults and twins than the lower-order alloys under identical tests.
The quinary alloy will exhibit a superior work-hardening response relative to the quaternary and ternary alloys.
The predicted microstructural behavior will produce greater strength and ductility in the quinary alloy than in the lower-order alloys.
